open_points.subject: CLK-001 operation boundary
open_points.text: “An operation reads the clock once” and “that one instant supplies … every current-time comparison that decides the validity of those writes” do not define whether authentication/session resolution, authorization, and the resulting use case are one operation or separate operations.
open_points.question: Must a request that authenticates a session and then performs a timestamped mutation share one wall-clock reading across the guard and mutation, or may each module-level operation take its own reading?
options: The whole authenticated use case is one operation and shares one instant across session/credential checks and writes.
Authentication/authorization and the mutation are separate operations, each taking one wall reading.
Only the mutation owns the shared instant; authentication may read independently.
open_points.default_guess: Treat the whole use case, including validity checks that authorize its writes, as one operation sharing one instant; retain only the explicit audit-writer exception.

witness.initial: A staff session expires at 12:00:00.000000 UTC; the wall source will return 11:59:59.999999 and then 12:00:00.000001.
events: The staff member submits a work-payment registration immediately before expiry.
The session guard checks the session, and the payment use case writes WorkPayment.recorded_at.
outcomes: If guard and mutation are one operation, both use 11:59:59.999999; the request succeeds and recorded_at is before expiry.
If they are separate operations, the guard succeeds using 11:59:59.999999 and the mutation reads 12:00:00.000001, so the same request can still commit with recorded_at after session expiry.
witness.observer: The staff member or an auditor reading the payment timestamp.

open_points.subject: CLK-001 Required tests and audit-writer exception
open_points.text: The normative rule permits “the audit writer's reading of an appended record's occurred_at” as “the one further reading”, but the CLK-001 test requires showing “that the operation reads it once” and “that its portal-owned event timestamps equal that instant” without excluding the audit writer or AuditRecord.occurred_at.
open_points.question: For a mutation that appends an audit record, must the CLK-001 test count one wall-source read or two, and must occurred_at equal the operation instant or the audit writer's later instant?
options: Exclude the audit writer from the test's one-read count and timestamp-equality assertion; expect one operation read plus one audit-writer read.
Count the entire mutation as one read and give the audit record the operation instant.
Count two reads but still require both returned timestamps to be equal.
open_points.default_guess: Apply the explicit normative exception: expect one operation read plus one audit-writer read, and exclude occurred_at from event-timestamp equality.

witness.initial: The clock source is controlled to return instant T1 on its first wall read and later instant T2 on its second.
events: An administrator creates a viewer, writing the viewer's created_at.
The same committed action appends its required audit record through the audit writer.
outcomes: Under the normative exception, created_at is T1, occurred_at is T2, and the clock source is called twice.
Under the literal Required tests wording, the operation is expected to call the source once and every portal-owned event timestamp, including occurred_at unless excluded, is T1.
witness.observer: The CLK-001 test and anyone reading the audit record.
